newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GELINAS SCORES FOUR GOALS AS CANUCKS BURY COYOTES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GELINAS SCORES FOUR GOALS AS CANUCKS BURY COYOTES.

text.p: Martin Gelinas scored four goals in a career-best five-point performance as the Vancouver Canucks converted six of just 17 shots on goal in a 6-2 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes.
It was the second hat trick this month and first career four-goal game for Gelinas, who also had an assist, while linemate Russ Courtnall had a goal and three assists for the Canucks.
Gelinas scored twice in the first period and twice in a four-goal second as Vancouver built a 6-0 lead despite being outshot 33-17 by Phoenix.

Vancouver goalie Kirk McLean made 31 saves, turning back 11 shots in the first period, eight in the second and 12 of 14 in the final period, when Cliff Ronning and Jim McKenzie scored for the Coyotes.

Phoenix goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin faced just four shots in the first period, but gave up two goals. He was replaced in the Coyotes net by Parris Duffus at 11:11 of the second period with his team trailing 5-0 after after giving up Gelinas' fourth goal.
At Florida, Rob Niedermayer scored with 70 seconds left in overtime to lift the Panthers to a 3-2 win over the St Louis Blues, snapping a season-high six-game winless streak.
The Panthers squandered a two-goal third-period lead but pulled out the win when Niedermayer one-timed a pass from Per Gustafsson past St Louis goalie Grant Fuhr.
Brian Skrudland and Ray Sheppard scored the other Florida goals.
Brett Hull sent the game into overtime with his 38th goal when he tapped home Al MacInnis's shot with 1:49 left in regulation to knot the score at 2-2.

In Boston, Ray Bourque had a goal and an assist and Adam Oates added three assists as the Bruins ended their longest winless streak in more than 32 years with a 6-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Oates set up goals by Bourque, Ted Donato and a short-handed tally by Rob Dimaio as the Bruins won after going 0-8-2 in their 10 previous games.
It was Boston's longest slump since going 0-11-1 from November 28-December 19 in 1965.
At New Jersey, the Toronto connection led the Devils to a second victory in as many nights, a 4-1 win over Buffalo that ended the Sabres' 12-game unbeaten streak.

Dave Ellett and Doug Gilmour, acquired Tuesday in a five-player trade with the Maple Leafs, each scored in a three-goal third period for the surging Devils, who improved to 8-1-7 in their last 16 games. Both played a significant role in Wednesday's win over the Islanders.
Ellett broke a 1-1 tie with a powerplay goal at 1:31 of the third. Gilmour added an empty netter in the final minute after Bill Guerin had put New Jersey in front 3-1.
In Detroit, Igor Larionov had a goal and two assists and Mike Vernon turned aside 29 shots as the Red Wings beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 4-1.
Vladimir Konstantinov added a goal and an assist and Bredan Shanahan set up a pair of goals as Detroit improved to 14-4-3 against Eastern Conference foes this season.
Vernon set the tone early by stoning Mario Lemieux on a breakaway just 15 seconds into the contest.
"If Vernon doesn't make that save, it could be a different game," said Red Wings coach Scotty Bowman.
At Colorado, Darryl Sydor and Joe Nieuwendyk each had a goal and two assists to lead the Dallas Stars to a 6-2 drubbing of the defending Stanley Cup champion Avalanche.

Neal Broten added a goal and an assist and Bill Huard and Pat Verbeek each had a pair of assists for the Stars, who set a franchise record with their 20th road victory and moved within four points of first-place Colorado in the Western Conference playoff race.
Mike Ricci and Eric Lacroix scored for Colorado, which suffered consecutive defeats for the first time since December 6-7.
In Los Angeles, Dimitri Khristich scored twice in the first period and Jeff Shevalier set up two goals in a three-goal second as the Kings beat the Edmonton Oilers 6-3.
Vladimir Tsyplakov and Jan Vopat each had a goal and an assist and Vitali Yachmenev picked up three assists for Los Angeles, which has its first four-game winning streak in almost four years.
Stephane Fiset finished with 29 saves for the Kings, including turning back all 14 shots he faced in the middle period. Andrei Kovanlenko scored twice for Edmonton in the third period.
